PullRequest.Title: Default new cloud automations to no allowed tools
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

New cloud automations now start with no allowed tools instead of selecting every tool in the catalog. Saving sends an explicit empty tools array without waiting for catalog loading. Editing or duplicating an automation preserves its saved tool selection, and edits with unreported tools preserve the existing configuration.

Updated dialog regression coverage for the default selection, selection labels and accessibility counts, explicit tool selection, and saving with ready, empty, loading, or unavailable tool catalogs.

No linked issue; requested as a default-behavior change.

### How to test

In the Agents window, open Customizations → Automations → Create Automation, turn on Run in the cloud, and choose a repository. Verify that the tools control shows zero tools allowed and the picker starts with every tool unchecked. Create an automation without changing tools, then verify its saved tool list is empty. Explicitly select tools and confirm those selections save; edit or duplicate an existing automation and confirm its saved selections remain selected.

### Validation

- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — failed because the `esbuild` dependency is missing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationDialog.test.ts --reporter dot` — not run because the preceding client build failed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/browser/automationDialog.ts src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationDialog.test.ts` — failed because the `eslint` dependency is missing.
- `npm run install-fast` — failed with `EALLOWSCRIPTS` (project-scoped `--allow-scripts` is rejected), blocking dependency restoration.

Manual UI validation was not performed.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A cold remote tool-catalog lookup was made a prerequisite of saving every new cloud automation that retained the default selection, keeping the save transaction and UI blocked for the full network duration even though the new default can be represented without the catalog.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Creating a cloud automation immediately after opening the dialog left the save UI busy and delayed the subsequent create request until `/automations/tools` completed; catalog failure also prevented progress.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The changed save path reads the already-initialized `selectedTools` value directly. New cloud automations initialize it to an explicit empty array, so saving no longer awaits the remote tool catalog; the existing dialog autorun may still load the catalog asynchronously for the picker, off the save critical path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, `getSessionConfiguration` called `resolveSelectedTools`, whose line 1946 awaited `waitForState(configuration.tools, catalog => catalog.kind !== 'loading', ...)`. This method runs inside `AutomationDialogService.save()` before `options.commit`, while the form is inert and the save button is disabled. The production provider implements `loadTools()` as an authenticated `GET /automations/tools`; it caches/coalesces loading and ready states, but a cold request still determines save latency. The replaced regression test explicitly showed that an early save remained pending until the catalog observable was set to ready.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and immediately save a new cloud automation while the tool catalog is ready, empty, loading, or unavailable
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Validation, automation-session synchronization, customization selection, and session configuration capture must finish before the unchanged automation create commit. The diff removes tool-catalog readiness from that critical path; catalog loading remains asynchronous UI support.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold request per account lifetime; loading and ready states coalesce subsequent calls, with another request only after an explicit retry following error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cold request was started on dialog open, and an early save additionally called the coalesced loader and awaited catalog transition before it could construct the create result.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The dialog still starts this request for picker data, but the changed save path no longer waits for it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the selected repository and fetch repository privacy/eligibility
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per distinct repository URI, cached in `targetEligibility` for the store lifetime until refresh/reset.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cached eligibility check before the change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Repository eligibility must resolve before save validation permits creation; unchanged by this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the cloud automation and publish the returned definition
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create mutation per accepted save.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One create request after catalog-dependent session capture completed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The actual persistence request remains on the save critical path, but can now start without waiting for tool-catalog readiness.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One save and one selected repository; catalog size n only drives an existing O(n) picker/control update when catalog data arrives, not save latency. The new serialized tools payload has cardinality zero by default.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The account-scoped tool request is coalesced by `cachedTools` while loading/ready and may overlap repository eligibility checking. The final create mutation is serialized by the provider operation queue; the diff does not add concurrency or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold tool catalogs issue one account-scoped request; ready and empty-ready results are cached, loading calls coalesce, and errors are retried only through the retry path. The new explicit empty selection is available independently of all cache states.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the old save awaited the catalog observable, the provider maps that state to a concrete network request, and the added line now reads initialized local state directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote catalog duration varies by account and network, but the removed await and its position before commit are explicit and were covered by the replaced pending-save test.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The change fixes eager remote work on the save critical path and adds only a constant-size empty array to the result.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the allowed-tools picker and explicitly change a new automation's selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The picker cannot open until the asynchronously loaded catalog is ready. Selection changes update local arrays and labels; saving then captures that local selection before the unchanged create request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the complete tool catalog in one GET request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request for all groups/tools on a cold account cache, regardless of tool count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request and picker gate existed; the previous default selected every returned tool.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to enable/open the picker, but not required merely to save the new default after this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number n of unique catalog tool IDs. Existing control updates and picker construction are O(n); the diff changes default checked state from n items to zero and removes one catalog-to-selection copy.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single coalesced catalog request supplies the whole picker. No per-tool network, IPC, filesystem, or subprocess work occurs; selection handling is synchronous in the dialog.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm account caches make the picker immediately ready; cold caches issue one request; failed caches expose retry. There is no per-item cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: picker construction, deduplication, and the provider cache are directly visible in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes vary, but the changed work is less than or equal to the prior path and no new expensive boundary scales with n.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; default-empty selection reduces checked-state and serialization work and preserves the single grouped network read.

Scenarios.Scenario: Edit an existing cloud automation, including definitions whose saved tools are unreported
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session synchronization and the unchanged guarded update remain required. Reported saved tools are copied locally and serialized on save; unreported tools leave `selectedTools` undefined so the existing configuration is preserved without catalog-dependent capture.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch catalog metadata for the tools control
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold account-scoped request, coalesced and cached.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dialog also loaded the catalog before; edits with unreported tools did not select defaults and preserved existing configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the save path after the change, including when saved tools are unreported.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the latest automation definition, then issue an update if the guarded patch is still applicable
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One authoritative GET and at most one update request per accepted edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both sequential provider operations remain on edit persistence's critical path and are unaffected by the changed tool-selection initialization.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Saved tool count k controls one shallow array copy and payload size. The diff preserves those costs and does not retain additional catalog or history state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Catalog loading is still a single coalesced background request. The provider update performs its authoritative read and update sequentially inside its mutation queue; the diff does not change that sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Catalog ready/empty states are cached per account; loading coalesces and failure can be retried. Existing reported selections are local snapshots; undefined remains the preservation sentinel for unreported edit state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: initialization explicitly distinguishes reported arrays from the edit-only undefined sentinel, and the update call path is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of saved tools varies, but no changed mechanism increases k-dependent work or boundary count.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression; the change preserves edit costs and removes only the obsolete select-all/wait path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Duplicate an existing automation with its saved tool selection
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The duplicate dialog initializes from the source session template, captures the copied selection locally, and then performs the unchanged create mutation. Tool-catalog readiness is not required to preserve the source selection.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch tool metadata for displaying/editing the copied selection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold request for the full catalog per account lifetime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was initiated; a stored tools array already prevented the old select-all wait path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not required for duplicate save after this diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One create request per accepted duplicate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical single create mutation with the copied session template.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Saved tool count k controls a shallow copy and create payload size, as before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One background, account-cached catalog load may overlap dialog work; one provider create mutation is serialized on commit.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm catalog data is reused; cold loading is coalesced. The saved selection is copied from the source and does not require reconstructing state from the catalog.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: duplicate passes the source session template into the same initialization and save path, while provider create behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Source selections may vary in size, but changed code neither increases their cardinality nor lifetime.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; selection preservation adds no new boundary or scaling work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance issue met the reporting bar. Recorded the removed cold tool-catalog wait as a high-confidence eager-work regression fix introduced by 6f8fb8a6b3457a9d17849b4c2cac0b2943924b86.
